goal: Staged senpi engine delta: expose original pre-transform user input as event.originalText to every input handler, make the engine inputId identity lifetime-unique, and add the single registered-tool effect lifecycle (synchronous tool_effect_before + promise-derived tool_effect_settled) at the tool wrapper immediately before definition.execute.

contract.originalText: Every input extension handler receives event.originalText = the original pre-transform user input text; it is constant across the handler chain while event.text stays the current (possibly transformed) text.
contract.inputId: inputId remains the single engine-generated identity shared by the input event and its later input_disposition event; the value is extended with a per-host-instance token so a recreated host of the same session can never regenerate an earlier inputId.
contract.toolEffect: One registered-tool effect lifecycle per session, owned by the ExtensionRunner: the tool wrapper (used for registered AND built-in tools) emits a synchronous non-swallowed tool_effect_before immediately before definition.execute - after every tool_call blocker and scheduler skip, so blocked/skipped calls emit zero effects - then exactly one tool_effect_settled derived from the actual definition promise (ok/isError/error; synthetic abort never settles early). Full shape and method names are published in EVENT-CONTRACT.md.
contract.fieldNames: New field names: originalText, tool_effect_before, tool_effect_settled (plus their event fields). Slot-4 already reads event.originalText and keys its journal on the opaque event.inputId, so no rename is required.

notes: All anchors are byte-exact against the pinned immutable base files; every expectedCount is asserted before any output write and a drift refuses with a nonzero exit.

Lifecycle emission point is the tool wrapper's execute (wrapper.js), which AgentSession uses for BOTH extension-registered and built-in tools; it is reached only after every tool_call blocker and scheduler/preflight skip.

tool_effect_before is synchronous and non-swallowed (a throw blocks definition.execute and yields zero settled); tool_effect_settled is emitted exactly once from the actual definition promise (not from tool_result and not from a synthetic abort). See EVENT-CONTRACT.md.

The bundled mirrors carry the identical contract; randomUUID aliases are the module-scope node:crypto bindings the bundles already use inside the agent-session module region (randomUUID11 in chunk-RRSND33J.js, randomUUID16 in session-worker.js).
The staged tree contains only these seven files plus manifest.json; it never duplicates the package and never touches pristine/, base/, the installed trees, or other lanes.
